meta.pointEstimateDefinition: The displayed margin is the posterior mean of the latent polling margin. The posterior is Gaussian, so the mean and the median are the same number. The 50%, 80%, and 95% intervals are central posterior intervals. They are not bootstrap percentiles and not a win probability.
meta.whyQ: The lowest future-consensus score was daily process SD 0.7 (excess SD 2.5, firm-shock SD 2.0, score 3.73). A 5000-draw bootstrap of races put the standard error of that score at 0.18. Process SDs inside that band, at the same excess and firm values, were [0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.85, 1.0]. The one-standard-error rule selects the smoothest of them, 0.1. Leave-one-cycle numerical minima were [0.6, 0.7, 0.85]. The 2026 Texas race was not in the objective.
meta.whyHalfLife: EWMA half-life 21 days had the lowest average 14-day future-poll RMSE (4.95 points) among 7, 10, 14, 21, 28, 35, and 42. The primary model does not use this half-life. Older polls lose influence because process noise accumulates.
meta.disclaimer: This is a polling-trend estimate, not a forecast and not a probability that either candidate wins.

modelLab.whyQ: The lowest future-consensus score was daily process SD 0.7 (excess SD 2.5, firm-shock SD 2.0, score 3.73). A 5000-draw bootstrap of races put the standard error of that score at 0.18. Process SDs inside that band, at the same excess and firm values, were [0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.85, 1.0]. The one-standard-error rule selects the smoothest of them, 0.1. Leave-one-cycle numerical minima were [0.6, 0.7, 0.85]. The 2026 Texas race was not in the objective.
modelLab.whyHalfLife: EWMA half-life 21 days had the lowest average 14-day future-poll RMSE (4.95 points) among 7, 10, 14, 21, 28, 35, and 42. The primary model does not use this half-life. Older polls lose influence because process noise accumulates.
modelLab.whyHouse: The house-effect prior SD is 3.42 points, the between-pollster standard deviation of mean residuals for pollsters with at least two polls in a race. A pollster with one poll is shrunk toward zero. This is not a partisan-bias label.
modelLab.objective: For each historical race, RMSE against the measurement-weighted consensus of independent pollsters in the windows 7–14 and 14–28 days after each checkpoint. Individual future-poll RMSE, MAE, log likelihood, residual autocorrelation, and 50/80/95 coverage are reported beside that score. Checkpoints are 90, 60, 40, and 28 days before election day. When several daily process SDs are within one bootstrap standard error of the best score, the smallest process SD is used.
modelLab.excludedFromObjective: The 2026 Texas gubernatorial polls are not in this file and were not used to choose q or the EWMA half-life.
modelLab.dateLimitation: This file has one date per poll. Calibration treats that date as a one-day field window. The live Texas model averages the latent margin across the stored field dates.

selected.populationNote: The historical file does not label likely-voter versus registered-voter samples. No separate population variance was estimated. Registered-voter polls still enter the live model, and the shared excess variance is the non-sampling term.

audit.whyQ: The lowest future-consensus score was daily process SD 0.7 (excess SD 2.5, firm-shock SD 2.0, score 3.73). A 5000-draw bootstrap of races put the standard error of that score at 0.18. Process SDs inside that band, at the same excess and firm values, were [0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.85, 1.0]. The one-standard-error rule selects the smoothest of them, 0.1. Leave-one-cycle numerical minima were [0.6, 0.7, 0.85]. The 2026 Texas race was not in the objective.
audit.whyFast: Fast latent process SD 0.15 is the smoothest value above the primary SD whose 7-to-14-day consensus RMSE (4.39) is within one standard error of the best faster candidate. The band was [0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.85, 1.0].
audit.fieldDates: A multi-day poll is not placed on its midpoint inside the filter. The update uses the release day, or the last field day if that is later. Because the random walk has no drift, the expected average of the latent margin over the field dates equals the latent state on that update day. Disagreement inside the field window is added as process variance. The midpoint is only a chart label.
audit.recency: The primary model does not multiply polls by an exponential recency weight. The EWMA half-life is a comparison model.
audit.sampleType: Likely-voter and registered-voter multipliers are weights in the local-linear comparison. They are not in the primary observation variance. The historical file does not identify sample type, so no extra registered-voter variance was estimated.
audit.varianceFloor: The 2-point variance floor is tau in the comparison model's precision weight, 1 / (sampling SE² + tau²). It is not added to the primary model's observation variance. The primary non-sampling term is the calibrated excess variance.
audit.pollsterDependence: Every poll's observation variance includes the firm-shock variance. A later poll from the same firm within 7 days includes that shock again, once per poll in the window, so the later poll adds less information.
audit.bootstrap: The primary 50/80/95 intervals are the Gaussian state posterior. They do not depend on bootstrap draws. Bootstrap draws apply only to the local-linear comparison.
audit.houseEffects: House effects are normal, centered at zero, and shrunk by the historical prior. They are not a partisan-bias label.
